```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ldfreq)
```

## Install the code, then choose the data

**ldfreq's code is MIT licensed and its installation contains no third-party
reference datasets.** Core lexical-diversity measures, your own reference
tables, concordances and study tables work without downloading these resources.
The adapted TUBELEX tokenizer example retains its BSD-3-Clause code notice.

| Resource name | Use | Separate terms | Download |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tubelex` | English frequency/prevalence profiles | BSD-3-Clause | 2.56 MB |
| `nj8` | New JACET 8000 rank/level profiles | JACET permission and attribution | 0.05 MB |
| `morpholex` | English morphological worksheets | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 1.34 MB |
| `bnccoca` | Nation's Level 6 word families | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 0.52 MB |
| `morphynet` | Nine example derivational relations | CC BY-SA 3.0 | 0.01 MB |

The terms apply to the corresponding data. For example, obtaining MorphoLex
through a separate download does not remove its noncommercial restriction.
Installing or using the independent MIT code does not require MorphoLex.

MorphoLex's noncommercial condition concerns the intended use, not simply
whether a user works for a company or a university. Review that use against
the terms; commercial use may require separate permission from the rights
holder. Setting `accept_license = TRUE` does not grant additional rights.
See the [Creative Commons explanation](https://creativecommons.org/faq/#does-my-use-violate-the-noncommercial-clause-of-the-licenses).

The package also includes authored examples and numerical summaries of its
corpus studies. The small MASC-format example was written for ldfreq; it is
not an extract from MASC. The research summaries contain aggregate estimates
and distributions, not corpus text, token sequences, participant identifiers
or document-level score tables. The metric-selection guide identifies the
corpora and the conditions under which those summaries were calculated.

## Inspect first, download explicitly

```{r inspect}
lexdiv_resource_info("morpholex")[c("resource", "version", "license",
  "license_url", "notice_url", "download_bytes")]
```

Open the license and notice links and confirm that the terms fit your intended
use. Select only the resources you need. No download happens unless you make
this call with `accept_license = TRUE`:

```{r download, eval=FALSE}
lexdiv_download_resources("tubelex", accept_license = TRUE)
# Or select several resources after reviewing each one's terms:
lexdiv_download_resources(c("nj8", "bnccoca"), accept_license = TRUE)
```

The downloader verifies the fixed archive and every member before making the
cache available. Normal reads verify the required file and do not contact the
network. A previously verified resource is reused.

```{r use, eval=FALSE}
tubelex_profile(c("student", "learn", "unfamiliar"))
nj8_profile(c("student", "learn", "unfamiliar"))
morpholex_data(sheets = "All roots")  # requires the separate morpholex resource
bnccoca_data()
```

## Choose a cache location or work offline

```{r custom-cache, eval=FALSE}
options(ldfreq.resource_dir = "/path/to/my/reference-cache")
lexdiv_download_resources("tubelex", accept_license = TRUE)
lexdiv_resource_info("tubelex")
```

Alternatively set `LDFREQ_RESOURCE_DIR` before starting R. Without either
setting, the cache is under `tools::R_user_dir("ldfreq", "cache")`. It sits
outside the package library, so reinstalling the package does not erase it.
A different pinned resource version gets a different subdirectory.

For an offline computer, copy the complete cache from a machine where you
explicitly obtained it under the applicable terms, then select that cache
location. Include the license and provenance files. A partial or modified
cache is rejected. Inspect the returned `path`, remove that specific version
directory if you intend to replace it, and explicitly download again.

## Update from 0.4.x

Earlier versions bundled these snapshots. In 0.5.0.9001 their data bytes and
resource identities are unchanged, but they are stored separately. Calls such
as `nj8_profile()` without a supplied word list now require the explicit cache
setup above. Existing saved results remain readable. Caller-supplied word lists
and reference tables continue to work without downloads.

Record the resource version, source hash, coverage and citation with your
results. `citation("ldfreq")` cites the package; it does not replace citations
for the data and measurement methods.
